subject: general
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 11**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 11** of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship through legislation.
 
• It allows the Parliament to make laws concerning the acquisition, termination, and other matters related to citizenship.
 
• This article is part of Part II (Articles 5 to 11) of the Constitution, which deals with Citizenship.
 
• Using the powers under Article 11, the Parliament has enacted laws like the **Citizenship Act of 1955** and its subsequent amendments.
 
• While Articles 5 to 10 determine the citizenship status of individuals at the commencement of the Constitution, Article 11 enables future legislative actions on citizenship matters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part II of the Constitution:** It deals with the provisions related to citizenship from Articles 5 to 11.
 
• **Citizenship Act of 1955:** This law, enacted under Article 11, specifies the methods for acquiring, losing, and determining Indian citizenship.
 
• **Modes of Acquiring Citizenship:** The Citizenship Act provides five modes: by birth, descent, registration, naturalization, and incorporation of territory.
 
• **Amendments to Citizenship Act:** Significant amendments include the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, which introduced provisions for granting citizenship to certain persecuted minorities from neighboring countries.
 
• **Difference Between Articles 5-10 and Article 11:** Articles 5-10 primarily address citizenship at the time of the Constitution's commencement, while Article 11 grants the Parliament the power to legislate on citizenship matters post-constitution.
